narr: Deep monsoon moisture brought thunderstorms, heavy rain, and flash flooding across northern Arizona.
ev: A stream gauge showed a 7 foot rise on Beaver Creek in less than 15 minutes.
A wash in the Sedona area was flowing 8 to 10 inches deep.
White Valley Road (N8031) was completely washed out.
Tonto Natural Bridge State Park posted pictures of Pine Creek rising 4 feet between 5:47 PM and 5:52 PM.
Tees Toh Wash was flowing about 2 feet deep about one mile west of Seba Delki.
lsr: A VIDEO POSTED ON SOCIAL MEDIA SHOWED STRONG FLOW MOVING ALONG THE BLOODY TANKS WASH, RESULTING A STREET CROSSING THE WASH NEAR MACKEY CAMP TO BE COMPLETELY IMPASSABLE.
GIA-2002 REPORTING BLOODY TANKS WASH IN FLASH FLOOD STAGE.
OVER THE PHONE REPORT OF 8-10 INCH IN WASH.
STREAM GAUGE INDICATED A 7 FT RISE ON BEAVER CREEK IN LESS THAN 15 MINUTES.
TONTO NATURAL BRIDGE STATE PARK POSTED PHOTOS OF A 4 FOOT RISE IN PINE CREEK BETWEEN 5:47 P.M. AND 5:52 PM. ON FB.
TEES TOH WASH FLOWING WITH ABOUT 2 FEET OF WATER ABOUT 1 MILE WEST OF SEBA DELKI.
THIS IS A POST EVENT REPORT. A USGS STREAM GAUGE ON SYCAMORE CREEK ABOVE THE VERDE RIVER INDICATED A 2 FT RISE AT 8:45 PM MST. EVENT TIME OF FLOODING IS ESTIMATED.
